αἰήταο: Αἰήτης — Aeetes, Circe’s brother; masc. gen. sg., epic -αο (= Attic -ου)
αἰαίην: Αἰαῖος — Aeaean, of Aea (Αἰαίη νῆσος, Circe’s island); adj., fem. acc. sg., with νῆσον
αἰὲν: αἰεί — always, ever; adv., epic by-form αἰέν (Attic ἀεί)
αἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj., epic/dialectal by-form αἰ (used before κε)
αἴθοπα: αἴθοψ — fire-faced, sparkling (of wine, lit. αἴθω ’burn’ + ὤψ ’face’); masc. acc. sg. · also of smoke, masc. acc. sg. (αἴθοπα καπνόν ’fiery smoke’)
αἴθρη: αἴθρη — clear bright sky, cloudless air; fem. nom. sg.
αἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl. (αἵ μοι ἕποντο ’which followed me’) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό: fem. nom. pl. demonstrative ’they’ (ἔνθ’ αἵ γ’ ’there they’)
αὐτοὶ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’themselves’ · also intensive in agreement with an unexpressed ’we’: ’we ourselves’ (αὐτοὶ βῆμεν ’we ourselves stepped out’) · also in agreement with an unexpressed ’you’: ’you yourselves’ (αὐτοὶ δ’ ὀτρύνεσθε ’and you yourselves rouse yourselves’)
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’ · also intensive with a noun, masc. gen. sg.: ’Alcinous himself’ (αὐτοῦ Ἀλκινόοιο) · also reflexive intensive gen. sg. after a personal pronoun: σέο τ’ αὐτοῦ ’and of yourself’
αὐτός: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. sg.: ’he himself’ · also masc. nom. sg. with a 1st-person subject: ’myself’ (ἐγὼ … αὐτός)
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὰς: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. acc. pl.: ’the (ships) themselves’
αὐτὴ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. nom. sg.: ’she herself’, ’you yourself’ · also fem. nom. sg., of a thing: ’it itself’ (αὐτὴ δὲ χθαμαλὴ κεῖται ’and the island itself lies low’) · also intensive, 1st person: ’I myself’ (οἶδα καὶ αὐτή ’I know it myself’)
αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg.: ’himself’ · also masc. nom. sg. with a 1st-person subject: ’myself’ (ἐγὼν αὐτός) · also masc. nom. sg. with a 2nd-person subject: ’yourself’ (εἰδήσεις δὲ καὶ αὐτός ’you will see for yourself’)
αὐτῇ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. dat. sg.: ’for herself’ · also plain anaphoric pronoun referring to a thing, dat. sg. with ἐν: ’in it’ (ἐν αὐτῇ, of the ship) · also reinforcing a 1st-person pronoun: ’myself’ (ἐμοί περ αὐτῇ, μοι αὐτῇ ’for me myself’) · also reinforcing a 2nd-person pronoun: ’you yourself’ (σοὶ ὧδ’ αὐτῇ ’for you yourself’) · also dat. sg. of a thing, no ἐν, ’against it’ or ’against her’, with ποτικέκλιται (referent uncertain: pillar or queen) · also plain pronoun, dat. sg. with μίσγεται: ’with her’ (οὐδέ τις αὐτῇ μίσγεται ’nor does anyone consort with her’)
αὖθι: αὖθι — there, on the spot, right there; adv.
αὖτ: αὖτε (elided αὖτ’) — again, in turn, moreover; epic adv./conj.
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
βάλεν: βάλλω — throw, cast; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, in tmesis with ἀμφί: ’threw about’ · also in tmesis with ἐπί (βάλεν δ’ ἐπὶ ... ἑκάστῳ = ἐπέβαλε): ’threw over, cast upon’ · also in tmesis with παρά (πάρ … βάλεν = παρέβαλε): ’threw beside, set before’
βουλεύειν: βουλεύω — take counsel, plan, deliberate; pres. inf. act.; βουλὰς βουλεύειν ’to give counsel’
βροτὸς: βροτός — mortal, as opposed to a god; masc./fem. nom. sg.
βρώμην: βρῶμη — food, eating; fem. acc. sg.
βόσκει: βόσκω — feed, pasture, nourish; pres. 3 sg.
βῆμεν: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 1 pl., unaugmented (= ἔβημεν): ’we went, we embarked’ · also ’we stepped out’, in tmesis with ἐκ (ἐκ … βῆμεν = ἐξέβημεν ’we disembarked’)
γίγνεται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen, arise; pres. 3 sg. (χρεὼ γίγνεται ’a need arises’)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γλαφυρὴν: γλαφυρός — hollow, smoothly wrought; fem. acc. sg.
γλαφυρῆς: γλαφυρός — hollow, hollowed; fem. gen. sg.
γῆς: γαῖα (γῆ) — earth, land; fem. gen. sg., Attic form γῆς (Homer usually γαίης)
δάκρυ: δάκρυ — tear; neut. acc. sg., used collectively: ’tears’ · also elided δάκρυ’ = δάκρυα, neut. acc. pl. · also literal sg. with an attributive adjective, not collective: θαλερὸν δάκρυ ’a swelling tear’
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δαινύμενοι: δαίνυμι — feast; mid. pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’feasting’
δείξω: δείκνυμι — show, point out; fut. 1 sg.: ’I will show’
δεινοῖο: δεινός — dread, terrible; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
δεινὸν: δεινός — dread, terrible, awesome; masc. acc. sg. (δεινὸν χόλον ’dread anger’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with a neuter noun (κῦμα): ’dread’; can also be taken adverbially
διηνεκέως: διηνεκής — continuous, unbroken; adv. διηνεκέως: ’continuously, from end to end, at full length’
διὶ: Ζεύς — Zeus, chief of the gods; masc. dat. sg.
δυώδεκα: δώδεκα — twelve; indeclinable numeral, epic δυώδεκα (= Attic δώδεκα)
δύω: δύο — two; numeral, epic by-form δύω, indeclinable
δώματα: δῶμα — house, dwelling; neut. acc. pl. (plural for a single dwelling): ’house, home’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses and heroes
δῖαν: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. acc. sg. δῖαν, here extended to the sea (ἅλα δῖαν ’the heavenly brine’) rather than a hero · also of a place-name: Λακεδαίμονα δῖαν ’heavenly Lacedaemon’ · also of Dawn: Ἠῶ δῖαν ’heavenly Dawn’
δῶμ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. sg., elided (δῶμ’ = δῶμα)
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’ · also with opt., in a wish: ’if only’ (εἰ … ὁμοφρονέοις … γένοιο) · also ὡς εἰ + opt., ’as if’ (ὡς εἰ … ἱκοίατο ’as if they had come’)
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’) · also in the idiom εἰς ὅ (κε) ’until’: εἰς ὅ κεν … μιγήῃς ’until you mingle with’
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’) · also with opt., of an aim in view: ’in case, to see if’ (εἴ τινά … λάβοι ’in case he might catch someone’) · also in ὡς εἴ τ’ + opt., ’as if’
εἶεν: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 pl., in an indirect question: ’(who) they might be’ · also with κε, potential: ’would be’ (κ’ … εἶεν)
εὐρυπόροιο: εὐρύπορος — wide-wayed, with wide paths (εὐρύς + πόρος); adj., fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
εὐρὺν: εὐρύς — broad, wide; masc. acc. sg.
εὐχετόωνται: εὔχομαι — declare, claim, boast; pres. 3 pl., diectasis εὐχετόωνται (= Attic εὔχονται)
ζόφον: ζόφος — gloom, darkness (esp. of the west, where the sun sets); masc. acc. sg.
ζώοντες: ζώω (Attic ζάω) — live, be alive; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ζῶντες)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θαλερὸν: θαλερός — blooming, vigorous, swelling; adj., neut. acc. sg. (θαλερὸν δάκρυ ’a swelling tear’) · also masc. acc. sg. (θαλερὸν γάμον ’a flourishing marriage’)
θανάτοιο: θάνατος — death; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεάων: θεά — goddess; gen. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic θεῶν)
θεοὶ: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’) · also of a goddess (θεός is common gender) · also nom. sg. subject, of a god already introduced by epithets but not yet named: ’the god’
θοῇ: θοός — swift, quick (standing epithet of ships); fem. dat. sg.
θυμὸς: θυμός — heart, spirit, desire; nom. sg.
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
θύελλαι: θύελλα — storm-wind, whirlwind; fem. nom. pl.
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κέ τοι λύσῃ ’so that she may free’)
κίρκη: Κίρκη — Circe, the enchantress goddess; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg., address: ’Circe!’ (ὦ Κίρκη)
κίρκης: Κίρκη — Circe, the enchantress goddess; fem. gen. sg.
κακόν: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. sg.: ’a bad thing, evil’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal passive (κακόν τ’ ἀγαθόν τε τέτυκται ’whatever, good or bad, has come to pass’)
καλέουσι: καλέω — call, name; pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic καλοῦσι)
κατέδυ: δύω — sink, enter, go down into; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, augmented, in tmesis (κατά … ἔδυ = κατέδυ): ’went down into’ · also without tmesis, of the sun: ’set, went down’ (ἠέλιος κατέδυ)
κατέλεξα: καταλέγω — recount, tell in order; aor. 1 sg.: ’I told, recounted’
καταδύντα: καταδύω — go down, set; aor. part. masc. acc. sg. (ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα ’at the sun’s going down, at sunset’)
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’) · also + gen., ’down from’ (κατὰ πετράων ’down from the rocks’) · also + gen., ’all over, throughout’ (κατὰ σπείους κέχυτο ’lay spread all over the cave’) · also + acc., of the part grasped: ’by’ (κατὰ νῶτα λαβών ’taking him by the back’) · also + acc., ’on account of, on the business of’ (κατὰ χρέος ’on business’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ)
κείνη: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); fem. nom. sg.
κείνου: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. gen. sg.
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’ · also + subj. in a relative clause, prospective: ’who is to, who will’ (ἥ κεν ἄγῃσι ’(a wagon) that shall carry’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … δαινύῃ ’whenever you feast’) · also + subj. in the protasis of a condition after αἴ: ’if ever’ · also + opt., potential: ’might, may’
κνέφας: κνέφας — dusk, darkness, nightfall; neut. nom./acc. sg.
κοίλοιο: κοῖλος — hollow; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
κοιμήσαντο: κοιμάω — put to sleep; mid. lie down to sleep; aor. 3 pl. mid., unaugmented: ’they lay down to sleep’
κορυφὴν: κορυφή — peak, summit; fem. acc. sg.
κοῖλον: κοῖλος — hollow; masc. acc. sg. (κοῖλον λόχον ’the hollow ambush’, i.e. inside the wooden horse)
κρέα: κρέας — meat, flesh; neut. acc. pl., uncontracted (= Attic κρέα contr.)
κρατὶ: κάρη (κράς) — head; neut. dat. sg. (stem κρατ-): ’with the head’
κυανοπρῴροιο: κυανόπρῳρος — dark-prowed; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), with νεός
κῆτος: κῆτος — sea-monster (any large sea-creature, not necessarily a whale); neut. acc. sg.
κῦμα: κῦμα — wave; nom. sg. · also acc. sg. (identical neut. form), object of a preposition (κατὰ κῦμα ’over the wave’) · also acc. sg., direct object: μέγα κῦμα ’a great wave’
λῦσαί: λύω — loose, release, let go; aor. inf. act., used as an imperative: ’release!, let go!’
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάκαρες: μάκαρ — blessed, happy (esp. of the gods); masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. in address: μάκαρες θεοί ’blessed gods!’
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέθυ: μέθυ — wine; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg. (identical form), subject of a passive verb (μέθυ πίνετο ’wine was drunk’)
μέλανος: μέλας — black, dark; masc./neut. gen. sg.
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’
μέσσῳ: μέσος — middle, in the middle; masc. dat. sg., epic doubled-σ (= Attic μέσῳ): ’in the midst of’
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’ · also ’lest’ + subj. after a past verb of urging (κελόμην … μή … λάθηται ’I urged … lest he forget’) · also in a condition, ’if … not’ (εἰ … μή τίς σε βιάζεται) · also with an infinitive used as an imperative, a prohibition: μή μ’ … καταλείπειν ’do not leave me’
μελιηδέα: μελιηδής — honey-sweet; fem. acc. sg., uncontracted (adj. of two endings) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masc. noun (μελιηδέα καρπόν ’honey-sweet fruit’)
μετηύδα: μεταυδάω — speak among, address (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg.
μεῖζον: μείζων — greater, larger; neut. nom./acc. sg., comparative of μέγας
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοῖραν: μοῖρα — due share, what is fitting, portion, fate; fem. acc. sg. (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’)
μυρία: μυρίος — countless, numberless; neut. acc. pl. μυρία · also neut. nom. pl. (identical form), agreeing with a nominative: ’countless’ (ὀνείατα μυρία κεῖται)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
νήπια: νήπιος — without sense, foolish, childish; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’foolish things’
νεὸς: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. sg., epic-Ionic (= Attic νεώς)
νεῶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. pl. (= epic νηῶν)
νηί: ναῦς (epic νηῦς) — ship; fem. dat. sg. νηί
νηός: ναῦς — ship; gen. sg., epic (= Attic νεώς)
νηὸς: ναῦς — ship; gen. sg., epic νηός (= Attic νεώς)
νηῦς: ναῦς — ship; nom. sg., epic νηῦς
νοστήσαντι: νοστέω — come home, return; aor. part. masc. dat. sg.: ’to you having come home’
νύ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
οἰκία: οἰκίον — house, home (Homer only in neut. pl. οἰκία, collective, = Attic οἰκία fem. sg.); neut. acc. pl.
οἰσέμεναι: φέρω (fut. οἴσω) — bring, carry; fut. inf. act. in -έμεναι (= Attic οἴσειν): ’to carry’
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἴη: οἶος — alone, only; fem. nom. sg.
οἴκαδε: οἶκος — house, home; + directional suffix -δε: ’homeward, to one’s home’
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὐκέτ: οὐκέτι — no longer; adv., elided (οὐκέτ’ = οὐκέτι)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὕτω: οὕτω(ς) — thus, so, in this way; adv.
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg.: ’all’ (πάντα δῆμον ’all the people’)
πάντας: πᾶς — all, every; masc. acc. pl.
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πέλωρ: πέλωρ — monster, portent, huge creature; neut. nom. sg., also said of a person in apposition: ’monster’
πέτρας: πέτρα — rock, crag, cliff; fem. acc. pl.
πέτρη: πέτρη — rock, crag; fem. nom. sg.
πανημέριοι: πανημέριος — all day long; masc. nom. pl., used adjectivally where English has an adverb
παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, among; + dat. · also + gen., ’from, from the side of’ (παρ’ Ἴλου ’from Ilus’) · also + acc., of motion, ’past, along, beside’ (παρ’ Μίμαντα ’past Mimas’)
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’)
παρὲξ: παρέξ — beside, past, beyond; adv./prep. + acc., here adverbial with εἴποιμι: ’say otherwise, speak beside the point’
πατρὶ: πατήρ — father; masc. dat. sg., governed by ὁμοῖοι ’like’ · also masc. dat. sg. of the person told: ’to (her) father’ (ἀγγείλειε ... πατρὶ φίλῳ ’report to her dear father’) · also masc. dat. sg. in apposition to Zeus: Διὶ πατρὶ ’to father Zeus’ · also masc. dat. sg. of the god prayed to: εὔχεο πατρὶ Ποσειδάωνι ’pray to your father Poseidon’ · also masc. dat. sg. after παρά: ’beside (their) father’ (παρὰ πατρὶ φίλῳ)
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’) · also adverb of place, no case: ’round about’ (περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ’and round it a fence is driven’)
πλεόνεσσι: πολύς — much, many; comparative πλέων/πλείων, masc. dat. pl. πλεόνεσσι, epic -εσσι (= Attic πλείοσι)
ποθι: ποθι — somehow, somewhere; epic enclitic adv. (= Attic πού)
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολὺς: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. sg., grave accent, mid-clause form (χειμὼν πολὺς ’much winter storm’)
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
ποταμοῖο: ποταμός — river; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
ποτὶ: πρός — to, toward, against; prep., epic ποτί, here as preverb in tmesis (ποτὶ … βάλε = προσέβαλε) · also a plain preposition + acc., no tmesis: ποτὶ τοῖχον ’against the wall’ · also + dat. ‘against’ · also + dat., ’on, upon’: ποτὶ χθονί ’on the ground’
προΐειν: προΐημι — send forth; impf. 1 sg., epic (= Attic προΐην): ’I sent forward’
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
προτὶ: πρός (epic by-form προτί) — towards, to; prep. + acc.
πρυμνήσια: πρυμνήσιον — stern-cable (mooring rope); neut. acc. pl.
πρόπαν: πρόπας — all through, the whole; neut. acc. sg., of time (πρόπαν ἦμαρ ’all day long’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’)
πρῶτον: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’first’
πυκνοὶ: πυκνός — thick, close-set; adj., masc. nom. pl.
πόδας: πούς — foot; acc. pl., accusative of respect
πότνια: πότνια — lady, mistress (title of respect for a goddess); fem. nom. sg. · also of a mortal woman, a respectful title: ’revered, honoured’ (πότνια μήτηρ ’the honoured mother’)
πώ: πώ — yet, up to now; enclitic adv. (usually with a negative)
πᾶσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl.
πῆμα: πῆμα — woe, calamity, disaster; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., direct object: ’woe’
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’
σπέος: σπέος — cave, grotto; neut. nom./acc. sg. (an irregular neuter noun declined σπέος, σπείους, etc.)
σπείους: σπέος — cave, grotto; neut. gen. sg., epic σπείους (= Attic σπέους)
στᾶσα: ἵστημι — stand, set; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg. (root aor. ἔστην): ’having stood, standing’
σφεας: σφεῖς — they; epic acc. pl. pron.: ’them’
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also as adverb, ’together’, or as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: σὺν … κάλυψε = συνεκάλυψε ’covered up’; σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’ · also adverb ’along, with (us)’ construed with ἔχοντες, which takes the object (σὺν … χεῖρας ἔχοντες ’having hands along with us’)
σῖτον: σῖτος — bread, grain, the staple of a meal; acc. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’
τέ: τε — and; enclitic connective, also marks a standing fact (epic τε) · also in the idiom ὅ τε (= ὅτι) ’in that, because’, giving a reason: ὅ τέ με … ἀποβῆναι ἀνώγει ’in that he bids me step off’
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl., epic (= Attic αἱ): ’they’
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεύχεα: τεῦχος — tool, gear, armor, equipment; neut. nom./acc. pl.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τόξῳ: τόξον — bow; neut. dat. sg., instrumental: ’with the bow’
τότ: τότε — then, at that time; adv., elided (τότ’ = τότε)
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τύμβον: τύμβος — burial mound, grave-mound; acc. sg.
τύμβῳ: τύμβος — burial mound, tomb; masc. dat. sg.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’)
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’that, the’ (τὸ σῆμα ’that mark’) · also article-like before the adverb πάρος: ’as before’ (ὡς τὸ πάρος περ) · also article-like before an ordinal, adverbial: τὸ τρίτον ’the third time’ · also distributive, neut. nom./acc. sg.: τὸ μὲν … τὸ δὲ ’one thing … another’ · also article-like before the adverb πρόσθεν: ’formerly’ (τὸ πρόσθεν ὄλοντο ’died long before’)
τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg. · also fem. gen. sg. with the force of a relative: ’of which’ (τῆς ἕτερον μὲν θειλόπεδον ’of which one part is a drying-ground’)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun · also relative adv., ’where, in the place where’ (τῇ δή μοι ἐείσατο χῶρος ἄριστος) · also adverbial, ’in that (event)’, pointing back to a contest just named: τῇ δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπεκαίνυτο ’in that Euryalus in turn outdid all’ · also relative adv. of manner, with περ: ’in just the way that’ · also adv. of direction, ’thither, that way’ · also with a noun, article-like: fem. dat. sg. ’the’ (τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’)
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’ · also distributive, ’of the one … of the other’ (τῶν μὲν … τῶν δ’ ’of the one band … of the other’)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’)
φάνη: φαίνω — show; aor. pass. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐφάνη): ’appeared’
φέρον: φέρω — carry, bear; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἔφερον): ’used to bear’ · also ’carried, were carrying’ (φέρον ἐσθῆτα ’they carried the clothes’) · also impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφερον): ’I carried, I was carrying’
φέρουσιν: φέρω — bear, carry; produce (fruit); pres. 3 pl.
φίλος: φίλος — dear, dear one; masc. nom. sg. used as voc.: ’friend’ · also plain attributive adjective, not vocative: ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’)
φίλων: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. gen. pl. (φίλοι ’kin, dear ones’)
φαίδιμ: φαίδιμος — gleaming, glorious (epic epithet of heroes); masc. voc. sg., elided (φαίδιμ’ = φαίδιμε)
φαινομένηφι: φαίνω — show; mid. appear; pres. part. mid. fem. dat. sg. with epic -ηφι (= Attic -ῃ): ’appearing’
φθόγγον: φθόγγος — voice, sound; masc. acc. sg.
φορέουσι: φορέω — carry, bear (habitually); pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic φοροῦσι)
φωτῶν: φώς — man, mortal; masc. gen. pl.
φύγεν: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. 3 sg., no augment (= ἔφυγε)
φῶτ: φώς — man; masc. acc. sg., elided (φῶτ’ = φῶτα)
χέοντες: χέω — pour, shed; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
χοροί: χορός — dance, chorus; masc. nom. pl.
ψαμάθοισιν: ψάμαθος — sand; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀίδαο: Ἀΐδης (Ἅιδης) — Hades; masc. gen. sg., epic -αο (= Attic -ου): ’of/in Hades’ house’
ἀίδεω: Ἀΐδης — Hades; masc. gen. sg., epic -εω (= Attic Ἅιδου)
ἀγήνωρ: ἀγήνωρ — lordly, manly, proud; adj. (2-termination), masc./fem. nom. sg.
ἀγορεύσω: ἀγορεύω — speak out, declare; fut. 1 sg.
ἀκουέμεν: ἀκούω — hear, listen to; pres. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἀκούειν)
ἀκτή: ἀκτή — headland, shore; fem. nom. sg.
ἀμβροσίην: ἀμβροσίη — ambrosia, the fragrant food/substance of the gods; fem. acc. sg.
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’) · also + gen., ’about, concerning’ (ἀμφ’ Ἄρεος φιλότητος ’about the love of Ares’)
ἀμφίπολοι: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, attendant; fem. nom. pl. · also fem. voc. pl., address: ’handmaids!’
ἀμφιτρίτη: Ἀμφιτρίτη — Amphitrite, Poseidon’s consort; nom. sg.; by extension, standing for the sea and its creatures generally
ἀμφιτρίτης: Ἀμφιτρίτη — Amphitrite, a sea-goddess, sometimes standing for the sea itself; fem. gen. sg.
ἀμφοτέρωθεν: ἀμφότερος — both; adv. with suffix -θεν: ’on both sides’
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.
ἀποβρίξαντες: ἀποβρίζω — sleep soundly, sleep through; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having slept’
ἀπονόσφιν: ἀπονόσφιν — far away, apart from; adv./prep. + gen.: ’far from’ (φίλων ἀπονόσφιν ’far from his dear ones’)
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀχνύμενοι: ἄχνυμαι — be grieved, sorrow; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.
ἁλὸς: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. gen. sg. · also masc. gen. sg., with the masc. adjective πολιοῖο: ’of the grey sea’ (ἁλὸς πολιοῖο)
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἃ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; neut. acc. pl.: ’what things’ (ἃ μενοινᾷς ’what you desire’) · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: neut. acc. pl. ’his own’ (τὰ ἃ ἔργα ’his own tasks’)
ἄγετ: ἄγω — lead; pl. imper. ’come now!’, elided (ἄγετ’ = ἄγετε), addressed to a group
ἄκουσον: ἀκούω — hear, listen; aor. imper. 2 sg., + gen.: ’hear (me)’
ἄλλην: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. acc. sg.
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄνθρωποι: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; masc. nom. pl.
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄσπετα: ἄσπετος — unspeakable, untold, unutterable; neut. nom. pl.
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐείκοσι: εἴκοσι — twenty; numeral, indeclinable, epic prothetic ἐ- (ἐείκοσι = εἴκοσι)
ἐθέλῃσθα: ἐθέλω — be willing, wish; pres. subj. 2 sg., epic ending -ῃσθα (= Attic ἐθέλῃς)
ἐικυῖα: ἔοικα — be like, resemble; perf. part. fem. nom. sg., + dat.: ’likened to, having the appearance of’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκάη: καίω — burn; aor. pass. 3 sg., augmented (unaugmented κάη), in tmesis with κατά (κατὰ … ἐκάη = κατεκάη): ’was burned up, were burned up’
ἐκέλσαμεν: κέλλω — drive a ship ashore, beach; aor. 1 pl.: ’we ran (the ship) ashore’
ἐλθόντες: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having come’
ἐμείναμεν: μένω — stay, wait, wait for; aor. 1 pl.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐξερέεινεν: ἐξερεείνω — ask out, question closely; impf. 3 sg., epic
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπεπείθετο: πείθω — persuade; plpf. 3 sg. with impf. sense: ’was won over’
ἐπὴν: ἐπήν — when, whenever (= ἐπεὶ ἄν); conj. + subj. · also + opt. in a generalizing conditional clause, without a further ἄν/κε: ἐπὴν κρητῆρι μιγείη ’when it has been mixed’
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐρυθρόν: ἐρυθρός — red; neut. acc. sg. (νέκταρ ἐρυθρόν ’red nectar’) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masc. noun (οἶνον ἐρυθρόν ’red wine’)
ἐρύσαντες: ἐρύω — draw, haul; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having hauled up’
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐυῆρες: ἐυήρης — well-fitted, shapely (of an oar); neut. acc. sg.
ἑκάστῃ: ἕκαστος — each, every; fem. dat. sg.
ἑκάστῳ: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. dat. sg.
ἑλοῦσα: αἱρέω — take, take up; aor. part. mid. fem. nom. sg., unaugmented: ’having taken’
ἑτάρους: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); acc. pl.
ἑταῖροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl.
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’)
ἔνθεν: ἔνθεν — from there, thence; adv. of place, with suffix -θεν
ἔρεβος: Ἔρεβος — Erebus, the dark of the underworld; neut. acc. sg.
ἔσσεται: εἰμί — be; fut. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἔσται)
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg. impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also existential, ‘there is’ (ἔστι δέ τις πέτρη ‘there is a rock’)
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἕκαστα: ἕκαστος — each, every; neut. acc. pl. used substantivally: ’each thing, everything’
ἠέλιον: ἥλιος — sun; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted ἠέλιον (= Attic ἥλιον)
ἠελίοιο: Ἠέλιος — the Sun (god); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic Ἡλίου)
ἠοῖ: ἠώς — dawn; fem. dat. sg. ἠοῖ
ἠοῦς: Ἠώς — Dawn; fem. gen. sg. Ἠοῦς
ἠριγένεια: ἠριγένεια — early-born; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
ἠώς: ἠώς — dawn; fem. nom. sg. (personified Ἠώς, Attic Ἕως)
ἠῶ: ἠώς (Attic ἕως) — dawn; acc. sg., accusative of extent: ’on into the dawn’ · also acc. after πρός: ’towards the dawn, the east’ (πρὸς ἠῶ) · also direct object of a verb of waiting: ’(waited for) Dawn’ (ἐμείναμεν Ἠῶ δῖαν)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’ · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a pool of water (ἡ δὲ προσέπλαζε ’and it lapped up’)
ἡδύ: ἡδύς — sweet, pleasant; neut. acc. sg., attributive
ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’
ἡμῖν: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; dat. pl. ’to us’
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥμεναι: ἧμαι — sit; pres. inf., epic (= Attic ἧσθαι)
ἥρη: Ἥρη (Ionic/epic by-form of Ἥρα) — Hera, wife of Zeus; fem. nom. sg.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦλθ: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. 3 sg., elided (ἦλθ’ = ἦλθε): ’he came, he returned’
ἦλθεν: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’came’
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἦμος: ἦμος — when, at the time when; temporal conj.
ἰδών: ὁράω (aor. εἶδον) — see; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having seen’
ἵκετο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 sg.; where the metre makes the ι long, that is the augment, which the spelling cannot show; with short ι, unaugmented
ἵκηται: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. subj. 3 sg. (short ι; subjunctives take no augment)
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense · also relative ’where’ + indic.: ἵνα … καθεύδετον ’where the two are sleeping’
ὀιστεύσας: ὀιστεύω — shoot arrows; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having shot’
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’)
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁδὸς: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. nom. sg.
ὁμοῦ: ὁμοῦ — together, together with, at the same place; adv.
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary-sequence verb: ὄφρα ... ἕλοις/ἵκοιο ’so that you might take/arrive’ · also temporal + indic., ’as long as’ (ὄφρα μὲν … ἦν ’so long as it was’)
ὅθ: ὅθι (elided ὅθ’) — where; relative adv. of place (distinct from ὅτε ’when’, similarly elided ὅτ’) · also ὅτε (elided and aspirated ὅθ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — when; temporal conj.: ὅθ’ ἑὸς δόμος ἀμφεκάλυψε ’when his own house sheltered (me)’
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’)
ὅτις: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; masc. nom. sg., epic (ὅτις = Attic ὅστις)
ὠκεανοῖο: Ὠκεανός — Ocean, the river encircling the earth; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὥς: ὥς — thus, so; also (with κε/ἄν + subj.) ’so that, in order that’; adverb/conjunction · also introducing an indirect question: ’how’ (ὥς κε νέηται ’how he is to return’, after φράσσεται) · or ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τε · also causal, ’since, seeing that’ (ὥς οἱ ἐναργὲς ὄνειρον ἐπέσσυτο ’since a vivid dream had come upon her’) · also with κεν + opt., purpose: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also ὥς ’just as’, in ὥς περ (accented before enclitic περ) (ὥς περ ὑπέστης ’just as you promised’) · also ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic με (ὥς με κελεύεις ’as you bid me’) · also postpositive after its noun, comparative ’like’ (οἰωνῶν ὥς ’like birds’)
ὦκα: ὦκα — quickly, swiftly; adv., from ὠκύς
ᾗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. dat. sg.: ’for which, to which’ (referring back to the ship, νηῦς) · also ’on which’, of a road: τὴν ὁδὸν ᾗ δὴ ’the journey on which’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: ’his own’, fem. dat. sg., agreeing with ἀλόχῳ (ᾗ … ἀλόχῳ ’his own wife’)
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
ῥηγμῖνι: ῥηγμίς — the line of breaking surf, the beach at the waterline (ῥήγνυμι ’break’); fem. dat. sg.
ῥινοὶ: ῥινός — skin, hide; fem. nom. pl.
ῥοδοδάκτυλος: ῥοδοδάκτυλος — rose-fingered; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
ῥόον: ῥόος — current, stream, flow; masc. acc. sg.
